ref_extractions.title: Complementary roles of neural synchrony and complexity for indexing consciousness and chances of surviving in acute coma
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies post-cardiac arrest coma patients and auditory evoked potentials in acute coma. The dataset consists of 67 comatose patients recorded in the first day of coma. This is a completely different population (pathological consciousness impairment) and paradigm (auditory stimulation in coma) compared to the MAVIS dataset (healthy subjects performing multisensory detection tasks).
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Study uses a cohort of post-cardiac arrest coma patients; no mention of openneuro_ds004010 or multisensory attention paradigm.

ref_extractions.title: Brain health in diverse settings: How age, demographics and cognition shape brain function
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper analyzes resting-state EEG from 1298 subjects across multiple global centers studying how demographics and cognition shape brain function. It does not mention the MAVIS dataset (openneuro_ds004010) and uses a different paradigm (resting-state) compared to the multisensory detection task in MAVIS.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Multi-center resting-state EEG study; no reference to MAVIS dataset or multisensory detection paradigm.

ref_extractions.title: Spectral slowing in chronic stroke reflects abnormalities in both periodic and aperiodic neural dynamics
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper analyzes MEG data from 23 chronic stroke patients, examining spectral parameterization to understand aperiodic and periodic neural dynamics. The population (stroke patients) and modality (MEG) are different from the MAVIS dataset (healthy subjects, EEG), and there is no mention of openneuro_ds004010.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses MEG data from stroke patients; not the MAVIS EEG dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Resting-state oscillations reveal disturbed excitation-inhibition ratio in Alzheimer's disease patients
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper analyzes resting-state MEG data from 86 amyloid-confirmed subjects across the AD continuum plus healthy controls. The study focuses on E-I balance using DFA, aperiodic exponent, and functional E/I ratio. It does not use the MAVIS dataset (which is EEG, healthy subjects, multisensory task) and there is no mention of openneuro_ds004010.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses MEG resting-state data from AD patients; unrelated to MAVIS dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Modality-specific tracking of attention and sensory statistics in the human electrophysiological spectral exponent
